title: Vasaloppet Prep - Lower Body & Core Strength

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Flow smoothly between positions, synchronize breathing with movement. Focus on spinal mobility from neck to tailbone.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Control the rotation, maintain upright torso. Feel the hip opening in each position. Move with intention, not speed.

items.name: Band Pullaparts
items.cues: Use light resistance band. Pull apart with control, engage rear shoulders. Full range of motion before chest.

items.name: Bodyweight Squats
items.cues: Warm up the lower body pattern. Full depth, chest up, weight in heels. Activate quads and glutes.

items.name: Back Squat
items.cues: Focus on depth and control. Chest up, elbows forward. Drive through midfoot. This is your primary strength builder for skiing endurance.

items.name: Bent Over Row
items.cues: Hinge from hips, maintain neutral spine. Drive elbows back and up. Builds posterior chain power essential for ski poling.

items.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
items.cues: Each leg - control the descent, front knee tracks over toe. Address unilateral strength imbalances critical for ski technique.

items.name: Cable Core Press
items.cues: Press explosively from chest. Resist rotation - core stability is essential for maintaining form over 90km. Brace hard.

items.name: Back Extension
items.cues: Control the negative, avoid hyperextending at top. Protects lower back and strengthens posterior chain. Full range of motion.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Each side - move with control, maintain neutral spine. Engage core. Excellent for stability and body awareness.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Hold each side 45 seconds. Gently lean forward, feel the calf stretch. Prevents tightness from skiing movements.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Hold each arm 45 seconds. Gentle stretch, no forcing. Opens up anterior shoulders and chest.

items.name: Child's Pose
items.cues: Rest and breathe deeply for 90 seconds. Allow body to recover. Finish strong and ready for next session.

rationale: Building maximal and relative strength in lower body through heavy back squats and bent-over rows is critical for Vasaloppet 90km success. These compound movements strengthen the muscles used in the poling and pushing phases of cross-country skiing.

Incorporating unilateral work (Bulgarian split squats) addresses muscle imbalances and improves skiing efficiency. Core pressing builds anti-rotation stability essential for maintaining form over marathon distances.

RPE 6-7 intensity with adequate rest periods allows for quality strength work 53 days out from race. Timing this strength block before transitioning to more race-specific endurance work prepares the body for sustained power output.
